## The question

[Rotate one axis in matplotlib](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78137364/rotate-one-axis-in-matplotlib), asked by [Matthew Leingang](https://stackoverflow.com/users/297797/matthew-leingang) on Stack Overflow (2024-03-10; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I have some series x and y such that x+y ≤ 1. If I make a simple scatter plot it looks like this:
>
> [![scatter plot][q-1]][q-1]
>
>
> I'd like to transform this plot so that the angle between the positive x and y axes is 60 degrees rather than 90 degrees. Basically I want the fundamental region bounded by the origin and (1,0) and (0,1) to be transformed from an isosceles right triangle to an equilateral triangle. 
>
> Through various web searches (including [this tutorial](https://www.tutorialspoint.com/how-to-rotate-a-simple-matplotlib-axes)) this is the closest I can come up with:
>
> ```python
>
> import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
> from matplotlib.transforms import Affine2D
> import mpl_toolkits.axisartist.floating_axes as floating_axes
>
> fig = plt.figure()
> plot_extents = 0, 1, 0, 1
> transform = Affine2D().skew_deg(30,0).scale(1,0.8660254038)
> helper = floating_axes.GridHelperCurveLinear(transform, plot_extents)
> ax = floating_axes.FloatingSubplot(fig, 111, grid_helper=helper)
>
> x = [0.41729137, 0.31693662, 0.25544209, 0.13843966, 0.31218805,0.01035702, 0.4847026 , 0.11104309, 0.25144685, 0.18332651]
> y = [0.20372773, 0.5395082 , 0.6020569 , 0.19787512, 0.57743819,0.93317626, 0.43035489, 0.8235019 , 0.36000727, 0.24365175]
> ax.scatter(x,y)
> ax.set_xlim(-0.15,1.15)
> ax.set_ylim(-0.15,1.15)
> fig.add_axes(ax)
> ```
>
> But the result seems to keep the points where they are and only move the one axis.
>
> [![second attempt][q-2]][q-2]
>
>   [q-1]: VEGkY.png
>   [q-2]: 6IO37.png
:::

Thanks to @JohanC for the pointer to [his answer to a similar question](https://stackoverflow.com/a/68664166/297797). The part I was missing is that the axes' current transformation needs to be added to the desired transformation.

```python
r = np.random.rand(3,10)
x = r[0]/(r[0]+r[1]+r[2])
y = r[1]/(r[0]+r[1]+r[2])

fig = plt.figure()
plot_extents = 0, 1, 0, 1
transform = Affine2D().skew_deg(30,0).scale(1,0.8660254038)
helper = floating_axes.GridHelperCurveLinear(transform, plot_extents)
ax = floating_axes.FloatingSubplot(fig, 111, grid_helper=helper)


ax.scatter(x,y,transform = ax.transData + transform)
ax.set_xlim(-0.15,1.15)
ax.set_ylim(-0.15,1.15)
fig.add_axes(ax)
```

[![successful plot][1]][1]

I need to prettify it some more, but this solves the problem in the question.
